A three-hour debate between Leahy and Guillaume Verdon ('Beff Jezos'), founder of effective accelerationism. They clash over whether AI progress should be accelerated or controlled and what values should guide the future.
The landmark doomer-versus-e/acc debate, both sides at full length.

Miotti discusses 'A Narrow Path', the policy plan he co-authored, which proposes how to get transformative AI benefits without building uncontrollable systems. He covers licensing, compute limits and international institutions.
A detailed walk-through of a concrete AI policy blueprint.
Elmore explains on The Inside View what she means by an indefinite global pause on frontier AI and why she founded PauseAI US. She discusses protests, public opinion and objections to pausing.
The fullest statement of Elmore's case for a pause.

A debate between Elmore and California state senate candidate Greg Tanaka on SB 1047, California's frontier AI safety bill. They argue over whether the bill would protect the public or stifle innovation.
A rare head-to-head debate on a real AI safety bill.
Steve Hsu interviews Tallinn on Manifold about AI risks, his investments in AI companies and when AGI might arrive. Tallinn explains why he funds safety work and how his views have changed.
A compact overview of Tallinn's views.
In The Trajectory's AGI Destinations series, Tallinn argues for a pause before humanity 'births' AGI. He discusses what a good long-term future could look like and why we should not rush.
Tallinn on what future he actually hopes for.

A three-hour 80,000 Hours episode in which Heim explains why compute is the most governable input to AI. He covers chip supply chains, export controls, compute thresholds and how regulators could monitor frontier training runs.
The definitive deep dive on compute governance.

Anderljung explains on 80,000 Hours how to regulate cutting-edge AI models, based on his paper 'Frontier AI Regulation'. He covers licensing, safety standards, model evaluations and the challenges of regulating fast-moving technology.
The essential explainer of frontier AI regulation.
Anderljung interviews defence expert Paul Scharre about his book 'Four Battlegrounds: Power in the Age of Artificial Intelligence', covering military AI and US–China competition.
A GovAI conversation on AI and national power.
Boeree's TED talk on the dark side of competition in AI, explaining how races between labs can sacrifice safety.
A short, crisp explanation of the AI race problem.

After a long break, Miles reviews how fast AI moved from 2022 to 2024 and what that meant for the safety field. He explains why researchers' timelines shortened and what governments and labs started doing.
Miles's personal account of a turbulent year in AI.
Muehlhauser tells Singularity Weblog why superhuman AI is likely to arrive this century and why it matters.
Muehlhauser's early case for taking AI seriously.
Davidson explains on 80,000 Hours how quickly AI could transform the world, walking through his compute-centric takeoff model and the possibility of explosive growth.
The fullest explanation of AI takeoff speed modelling.
Part 1 of Shulman's 80,000 Hours series on the economy and national security after AGI.
A four-hour deep dive on the post-AGI world.
Part 2 of Shulman's 80,000 Hours series on government and society after AGI, including AI advisers and epistemics.
How institutions could change with AGI.
Zvi Mowshowitz joins 80,000 Hours for a three-hour tour of the biggest AI updates since ChatGPT, including the 'sleeper agents' paper, lab safety policies and what to expect next.
A dense catch-up on AI safety developments.
On Hidden Forces, Suleyman discusses artificial intelligence and the containment problem.
A focused discussion of containment.
Intelligence Squared hosts Suleyman in conversation with The Economist's Zanny Minton Beddoes about The Coming Wave.
A polished public conversation on the book.
Dwarkesh Patel interviews Demis Hassabis on scaling, superhuman AI, combining search with LLMs and the safety challenges of AGI.
A technical interview including Hassabis's safety views.
Hassabis's 'Unreasonably effective AI' lecture on DeepMind's science and his approach to responsible AGI development.
Hassabis's vision for AI, with safety framing.

Lecture 1 of the Center for AI Safety's 'AI Safety, Ethics & Society' course gives a structured overview of catastrophic AI risks. It sorts them into malicious use, AI races, organisational accidents and rogue AIs, matching the course textbook.
The cleanest one-hour map of the whole risk landscape.
MLST: Akbir Khan, lead author of the ICML 2024 best paper 'Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers', explains how debate between models helped weaker judges find the truth.
The empirical evidence that debate can work.
AXRP 33: Scott Emmons explains how RLHF can go wrong when human evaluators only partially observe what the model does, which can reward deceptive or overjustifying behaviour.
A rigorous look at why RLHF alone isn't enough.
AI, Government, and the Future podcast: Heim, then at the Centre for the Governance of AI, discusses the future of compute governance and practical policy options.
Policy-focused follow-up on compute governance.
Dan Hendrycks' Berkeley EECS lecture gives an AI safety primer and then explains representation engineering: reading and steering high-level concepts like honesty directly in a model's activations.
Top-down interpretability from the director of CAIS.
Cornell mathematician Lionel Levine's Isaac Newton Institute talk (31 Oct 2024) on what mathematics can contribute to AI safety and which problems mathematicians could take on.
A mathematician's invitation into safety research.
At the Simons Institute, Sarah Schwettmann introduces Automated Interpretability Agents that design and run experiments on models to explain their behaviour.
The core idea behind Transluce's tools.

The September 17, 2024 Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing with former OpenAI and Google insiders – William Saunders, Helen Toner and Margaret Mitchell – plus David Evan Harris. They describe safety culture problems inside AI labs and call for whistleblower protections and oversight.
Landmark insider testimony.
An invited UCL DARK talk by Adam Gleave on the adversarial robustness of superhuman AI systems, centred on attacks against superhuman Go agents.
The technical version of the Go-exploit story.
FAR.AI seminar on deceptive instrumental alignment and how Anthropic builds model organisms to study it.
Up-to-date research talk.

Daniel Filan interviews Beth Barnes about what evals are, how good they are, whether models show their full capabilities, and METR's policy work. A thorough technical look at evaluating dangerous capabilities.
A careful technical primer on frontier-model evaluations.

Jan Leike (Anthropic) presents 'Supervising AI on hard tasks' at the July 2024 Vienna Alignment Workshop. He explains why supervising models on tasks humans can't check is the central problem and reviews current approaches.
Short state-of-the-field talk on scalable oversight.
Neel Nanda (Google DeepMind) gives 'Mechanistic Interpretability: A Whirlwind Tour' at the July 2024 Vienna Alignment Workshop. A fast, well-organised survey of methods and open problems.
Fast, clear overview.
Alex Kantrowitz talks with Saunders and Lawrence Lessig about what ex-OpenAI safety staff are worried about.
Saunders explains the 'Titanic' worry.
Batson and Anthropic's interpretability team on the engineering behind scaling interpretability.
Behind the scenes of scaling SAEs.
Technical talk to physicists at Strings 2024 (CERN) asking whether human-level AI is coming by 2030.
Physicist-level reasoning about AI timelines.
Four-hour Dwarkesh interview on 2027 AGI, trillion-dollar clusters, CCP espionage, his OpenAI firing and superalignment.
The essential 'Situational Awareness' conversation.

Lex Fridman podcast #431 with Roman Yampolskiy, author of 'AI: Unexplainable, Unpredictable, Uncontrollable'. He argues superintelligent AI may be impossible to control and explains his very high estimate of catastrophe.
The fullest treatment of his impossibility arguments.
Schulman on how post-training tames models, reasoning, and how labs should coordinate if AGI arrives early.
Thoughtful on safety and coordination.
In this Sana Strange Loop interview Hinton reflects on the journey from early neural networks to today and on AI's limits and potential. He discusses reasoning, understanding and risk.
A thoughtful career retrospective with forward-looking warnings.
Chris Williamson asks Bostrom whether we are headed for AI utopia or disaster. Bostrom discusses his book Deep Utopia and what a solved world might mean for human purpose.
Covers both the risk and the upside of advanced AI.
Alex O'Connor interviews Bostrom about AI ethics, including why deceiving AI might backfire on us. They discuss digital minds and moral status.
Focus on AI moral status and how we treat AI.
UnHerd's Flo Read meets Bostrom to discuss how AI could lead to tyranny and the risks of surveillance and concentrated power. Bostrom reflects on a year of rapid AI progress.
Political and governance risks of AI.
Tom Bilyeu interviews Bostrom on the future of AI, humanity and utopia versus dystopia. Bostrom predicts life will get weird over the next few years.
An accessible look at near-term change.
In a 2023 TED talk Tegmark explains how to keep AI under control. He argues for provably safe systems instead of hoping alignment works.
His short pitch for provably safe AI.
In a Sana Strange Loop session, Tegmark discusses what we cannot ignore in the AI revolution. He covers control, regulation and optimistic paths.
A thoughtful mid-length conversation.

The Institute of Art and Ideas' full interview with Aaronson on AI, consciousness, quantum physics and AI safety. He discusses what threats AI could pose and whether seeming to understand is understanding.
A thoughtful overview of his AI views.
Curt Jaimungal interviews Aaronson, then at OpenAI, about future scenarios for AI. They discuss different possible worlds and safety.
Insider perspective from his OpenAI years.
In a TEDxPaloAlto talk Aaronson confronts the idea of human specialness in the age of AI. He asks what, if anything, will remain uniquely human.
A short, provocative talk.
Lawrence Krauss talks with Aaronson for three hours, from quantum computing to AI safety. Aaronson explains his OpenAI watermarking work.
A long tour of his career.
A Berkeley EECS lecture, 'Using AI to understand AI', on automated interpretability. Steinhardt shows how models can explain other models.
Introduces the idea behind Transluce.
A Schwartz Reisman Institute seminar arguing you can't have AI safety without inclusion. Hadfield-Menell connects alignment to whose values count.
Links technical alignment to social questions.
At an MIT Schwarzman College of Computing event on multimodal AI, Hadfield-Menell gives a talk on his research. He discusses alignment challenges for new AI systems.
Short academic talk.
On the Google DeepMind podcast, Hannah Fry talks with Dragan about AI safety and whether worries are 'doomer'. Dragan explains how DeepMind approaches building safe models.
Her view as DeepMind's safety lead.
A Concordia AI session where Christiano explains eliciting latent knowledge (ELK). He discusses getting AI to report what it knows.
Introduction to ELK by its originator.
Dwarkesh Patel and Carlsmith discuss preventing AI takeover, trusting power and avoiding authoritarian urges to control. They draw on his 'Otherness and control' essays.
His most-watched long conversation.

Joe Carlsmith lectures at Stanford's CS 362 (Research in AI Alignment) on his essay series 'Otherness and control in the age of AGI'. He examines when it is right to control AI systems and the tension between control and respect for other minds.
Lecture on his major essay series.
Cognitive Revolution's Nathan Labenz discusses with Grace the survey of 2,700+ AI researchers on the future of AI. They go through key findings.
The survey's results explained.
On FLI, Grace discusses the largest survey of AI researchers to date and their beliefs about risks and timelines.
Survey results on expert expectations.
EYE4AI interviews Grace on when AI will surpass humanity. She explains forecasts in accessible terms.
Accessible timelines introduction.
The DemystifySci Podcast asks Grace how worried we should be about AI. A long, wide-ranging conversation.
Long-form general discussion.
An 80,000 Hours episode on the most important century for humanity: will the future be wild or boring?
Core thesis of his writing.
At Cerebral Valley, Casey Newton interviews Karnofsky, then director of AI strategy at Open Philanthropy. A short discussion of AI risk and strategy.
A brief industry-event interview.
At TED, Legg and Chris Anderson discuss the transformative potential of AGI and when it might arrive.
A short TED conversation.
Legg speaks at USI's 28th Dies academicus on the future of artificial intelligence.
Short academic address.
Machine Learning Street Talk interviews Shanahan about LLMs as role-players and the 'monsters' inside them. He explains his role-play framing.
His key paper explained.
Mind-Body Solution discusses conscious exotica and the space of possible minds with Shanahan.
The space of possible minds.
A Virtual AI Safety Unconference 2024 session on provably safe AI led by Omohundro.
Discussion of formal-verification safety.
A SingularityNET BGI session where Omohundro talks about provable technology for beneficial AGI.
Concise provable-safety pitch.
A Schwartz Reisman Institute seminar on social choice and game theory for AI alignment by Conitzer.
Social choice approach to alignment.

Russell's April 2024 Neubauer Collegium lecture 'AI: What If We Succeed?' asks whether recent advances put AGI within reach and what happens if they do. He explains how to keep control of systems more capable than us.
A polished recent lecture on the central question of his career.

At the Hoover Institution and Stanford HAI 'Policy Challenge of AI Safety' event, Leung (then CTO of the UK AI Safety Institute) joins Henry de Zoete and Ollie Ilott to report on building the world's first AI Safety Institute. They describe how the institute tests frontier models.
A first-hand account of how the UK AISI was built.
IAIFI fireside chat with Kaplan on generative AI's impact on the physical sciences.
Physics-to-AI perspective.
Perez presents Sleeper Agents: deceptive LLMs whose backdoors persist through supervised fine-tuning, RLHF and adversarial training.
Primary-source talk on Sleeper Agents.
The Inside View: Hubinger on the 'Sleeper Agents' paper (backdoored deceptive models survive safety training) and on Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy.
Accessible walkthrough of Sleeper Agents.

Garfinkel scrutinises the classic arguments for AI existential risk on 80,000 Hours, explaining which parts he finds convincing and which he thinks have not been fleshed out. He discusses alternative routes by which AI could still be a big deal.
The best-known sceptical-but-serious look at AI risk arguments.
Collin Burns presents OpenAI's weak-to-strong generalization result at the New Orleans Alignment Workshop: can a weak model's labels train a stronger model to perform beyond its supervisor?
Short talk on a key Superalignment result.

Spencer Greenberg talks with Buck Shlegeris about how to form true beliefs, enjoy being wrong, and present claims honestly. It is a wide-ranging conversation on reasoning habits rather than AI specifics.
Shows the thinking style behind Buck's research choices.
An early long-form conversation with Alex Meinke, then an independent researcher, about existential risk, alignment and interpretability.
Meinke's views before joining Apollo.
Jeffrey Ladish explains the 'security mindset' and applies it to AI and existential risk, from his time running a security consultancy.
Early statement of a lasting theme.
Eli Lifland, then with the Samotsvety forecasting group, discusses AI alignment strategy, power-seeking risk and forecasting with QURI.
Lifland's views before AI 2027.
Dan Hendrycks discusses whether an AI arms race has begun and the competitive pressures that drive risky AI development.
Accessible take on racing dynamics.
Dan Hendrycks argues evolutionary dynamics favour selfish AIs over humans and discusses how to develop AI safely despite those pressures.
His 'natural selection favors AIs' argument in full.
Dan Hendrycks surveys AI safety research directions at the 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop.
Compact map of research areas.
Jaime Sevilla presents Epoch AI's work on AI trends for an Apart hackathon.
Short intro to Epoch's data.
An early Inside View interview with Jesse Hoogland about AI risk and interpretability, before Timaeus.
Hoogland's starting point.
Daniel Murfet makes the case for short AGI timelines in a metauni talk.
Why a mathematician switched to AI safety.
A special MLST episode with Christopher Summerfield on 'Natural General Intelligence' and what neuroscience and AI teach each other.
Deep neuroscience-AI crossover.
Owain Evans, then at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute, presents work on truthful language models and alignment.
His TruthfulQA-era research.
Stephen Casper argues interpretability research should be judged by whether it helps engineers do useful things, like finding and fixing model flaws.
His influential critique of interpretability.
Vanessa Kosoy lectures on reinforcement learning theory at an agent foundations workshop.
Mathematical background for her agenda.
Abram Demski lectures on the partition assumption in decision theory at an agent foundations workshop.
Classic agent-foundations material.
Steven Byrnes presents the challenges for safe and beneficial brain-like AGI at a Foresight Institute seminar.
Talk version of his agenda.
Steve Byrnes gives the same core talk on safe brain-like AGI in the PIBBSS speaker series, with different Q&A.
Alternative version with PIBBSS audience.

An in-person, long-form MLST interview where Leahy lays out why he thinks AGI is coming soon and why it is likely to go badly by default. He covers alignment difficulty, the AI race, Conjecture's approach and what a sane response would look like.
The deepest single interview with Leahy on why he expects AGI to be dangerous.

A live MLST conversation between Leahy and cognitive scientist Joscha Bach on whether superintelligent AI will be dangerous. Bach is more relaxed about AI succeeding humanity; Leahy pushes back hard on that view.
See Leahy argue with one of the most original thinkers on machine minds.
On the crypto podcast Bankless, Leahy explains to a general audience why he thinks AI is a 'ticking time bomb'. He discusses alignment, why the labs keep racing and what ordinary people can do.
A clear introduction to the AI risk argument for newcomers.
A live MLST debate between Leahy and hacker-entrepreneur George Hotz on AI safety. Hotz argues decentralised, open AI is safer; Leahy argues uncontrolled capability is the danger.
A fast, combative debate on open versus controlled AI.
Daniel Filan interviews Elmore on The Filan Cabinet about the case for an AI pause and her move from effective altruism research into activism. They dig into the strategy and ethics of protest.
A thoughtful, probing interview on why she became an activist.
Logan Bartlett interviews Tallinn about his career from Skype to AI safety, his investments and the risks of advanced AI. They also discuss his early donation to FTX-related projects.
A broad biographical interview.
On the FLI podcast Heim introduces compute governance: why chips are measurable, excludable and concentrated, and what policies this makes possible.
A shorter introduction to compute governance.
Heim explains the 'AI triad' of compute, data and algorithms and how each drives AI progress. He discusses trends in training compute and what they mean for forecasting and policy.
A clear primer on what makes AI systems more capable.
An early long interview with Heim on AI compute governance, his path into the field and open research questions.
Good background on how compute governance emerged.
A GovAI webinar on how frontier AI models should be regulated, with Anderljung and co-authors discussing the 'Frontier AI Regulation' paper and taking questions.
Hear the authors of a key regulation paper debate the details.
Harris's CogX Festival 2023 talk 'Beyond the AI Dilemma', updating his argument after a year of rapid AI deployment and discussing governance solutions.
A follow-up to The AI Dilemma with policy ideas.
Liv Boeree and Daniel Schmachtenberger discuss Moloch, AI and capitalism – how competitive pressures drive harmful outcomes and how AI could accelerate them.
The deepest exploration of the 'Moloch' frame for AI.
On the FLI podcast Boeree discusses lessons from poker, GPT-4 and the future of AI, including game theory, risk and competitive dynamics.
Boeree on how a poker mindset applies to AI risk.
On MLST Miles explains why 'there is a good chance this kills everyone', covering misalignment, instrumental convergence and reasons for concern.
A clear, technical-yet-accessible case for concern.
Miles discusses ChatGPT on Computerphile: how it was trained with human feedback, its limitations and what it means for alignment.
Understand RLHF and ChatGPT from a safety angle.
Spencer Greenberg asks Rob Miles why alignment is a problem at all, why video works for explaining research, and which solutions seem promising.
Miles on what might actually work.
On the FLI podcast Davidson explains how quickly AI could automate the economy and what his model says about takeoff.
An accessible introduction to his takeoff model.
A GovAI talk by Davidson on what a compute-centric framework says about AI takeoff speeds.
The original presentation of his takeoff report.
Part 1 of Dwarkesh's seven-hour conversation with Carl Shulman. Shulman explains the intelligence-explosion argument, robot-economy doubling times and evidence from primate evolution.
One of the most influential AI interviews ever recorded.
Part 2 of the Shulman interview covers how an AI takeover could unfold, bio and cyber attack routes, how to detect deception in AI systems and what humanity's long-term future could look like.
Shulman's detailed picture of how AI takeover could happen.
On the Futurati Podcast in 2023, Zvi discusses whether we should halt progress in AI.
A short early take on pausing AI.
Marcus's 2023 TED talk on the urgent risks of runaway AI and his proposal for a global, neutral AI governance body.
Marcus's policy proposal in 14 minutes.
MLST discusses the 2023 Senate hearing with Marcus, who explains his testimony and his views on Sam Altman and AI regulation.
Behind the scenes of the 2023 Senate hearing.
Sam Harris asks Mustafa Suleyman whether we can contain artificial intelligence, discussing his book 'The Coming Wave' and the containment problem.
Suleyman's containment thesis, explored in depth.
Suleyman tells The Diary of a CEO that AI is becoming more dangerous and threatening, explaining the containment challenge.
His most-watched long interview on AI risk.
A full debate between Suleyman and Yuval Noah Harari, hosted by The Economist, on what the AI revolution means for humanity.
Two big thinkers on AI's impact on humanity.
Suleyman explains on 80,000 Hours how to get Washington and Silicon Valley to tame AI.
Suleyman's policy ideas for containing AI.

Dan Hendrycks' full Introduction to ML Safety course, published as one long video by freeCodeCamp. It covers robustness, anomaly detection, interpretability, honesty, power-seeking and systemic safety with ML-level detail.
A complete university-style ML safety course in one sitting.
AXRP 19: Daniel Filan and Neel Nanda go deep on how well we understand models' internal computation, including induction heads, the grokking modular-addition circuit and research methodology.
The technical deep-dive companion to his explainers.

Part 1 of Nanda's walkthrough of his paper 'Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability', with his co-author. It explains how a small transformer learns modular addition with Fourier features.
A hands-on example of fully reverse-engineering a network.
MLST: Connor Leahy (Conjecture) and George Hotz debate whether we can develop truly beneficial AI, covering open source, power concentration and alignment difficulty.
A safety researcher vs a hacker-accelerationist.
AXRP 20: Scott Aaronson on 'reform' AI alignment (taking risks seriously without assuming doom), his watermarking work at OpenAI and what theoretical computer science can offer.
A famous theorist's moderate view of alignment.
The Inside View turns the tables on AXRP host Daniel Filan, then a UC Berkeley PhD candidate, asking about his podcast, his views on LLMs and his interpretability work.
Meet the host behind dozens of the best researcher interviews.
Vasant Dhar talks with Bowman about ChatGPT, how language models work and how we stay in charge of increasingly capable AI.
Accessible conversation for newcomers.
Stanford MLSys seminar where Kaplan covers Anthropic's early alignment research: helpful-harmless RLHF, self-supervision and scaling.
Technical view of Anthropic's early safety work.
Bloomberg Live interview on the optimistic case for AI and how Anthropic pairs it with safety.
Short balanced overview.
Four-hour MLST interview with Neel Nanda covering grokking, Othello-GPT's world model, superposition and how he thinks about doing interpretability research.
Exhaustive technical interview.
The Inside View interview on mechanistic interpretability, superposition and grokking.
Conversational technical primer.
FLI podcast on how mechanistic interpretability could help avoid an AI catastrophe.
Safety-motivated case for interpretability.
SERI MATS talk on concrete open problems in mechanistic interpretability for new researchers.
Research agenda for newcomers.
Pieter Abbeel's Robot Brains podcast on ChatGPT's invention, capabilities and limitations.
Origin story of ChatGPT.
Kirchner shows how he uses Elicit to draft a research proposal in two days.
Practical research workflow.

The Inside View with Collin Burns, then a Berkeley PhD student with Jacob Steinhardt. He explains 'Discovering Latent Knowledge': finding truth-like directions in a model's activations without labels, as a step toward honest AI.
Deep dive on eliciting truth from models.
Aschenbrenner and Richard Hanania argue AI alignment is a solvable problem.
His alignment optimism, pre-OpenAI essays.
Increments podcast debate on whether the end is nigh with superintelligence.
Debate with sceptics.

Dwarkesh Patel and Paul Christiano, inventor of RLHF and founder of the Alignment Research Center, discuss how an AI takeover could happen and how to prevent it. Topics include whether he regrets RLHF, what a good post-AGI world looks like and ARC's theory work.
His most-watched and comprehensive interview.
Recorded in October 2023, Hinton is joined by Fei-Fei Li at the University of Toronto for a conversation on responsible AI development. They agree and disagree on risks and priorities.
Two AI pioneers with different emphases on risk.
Leike's 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop talk on scaling reinforcement learning from human feedback, including where RLHF breaks down as models surpass their supervisors.
Insider account of RLHF's strengths and limits.

Jan Leike explains OpenAI's 2023 Superalignment plan: put 20% of compute behind aligning superintelligence within four years, largely by building an automated alignment researcher. He discusses scalable oversight, interpretability and why he was optimistic.
The definitive long-form explanation of the Superalignment bet.
Dwarkesh Patel and Amodei discuss why scaling works, alignment, bioweapon misuse, lab security and Anthropic's mission.
Classic 2023 interview with deep risk discussion.

80,000 Hours (originally July 2023): Holden Karnofsky argues AI doesn't need to be superintelligent to take over; many human-level AIs could be enough. He then sets out a practical playbook for labs and governments.
His AI safety playbook explained.

Mark Xu explains mechanistic anomaly detection: flagging when a network produces an output for an unusual internal reason, as a defence against treacherous turns. They also discuss formalizing heuristic arguments.
The main recorded explanation of ARC's anomaly-detection agenda.

Daniel Filan presses Jan Leike on the details of Superalignment: what an automated alignment researcher is, how to validate it and what could go wrong. A technical companion to his 80,000 Hours episode.
Most technical interview on the Superalignment agenda.

The July 25, 2023 Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI oversight and regulation, with testimony from Stuart Russell, Yoshua Bengio and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. They warn about near-term misuse such as bioweapons and the need for binding rules.
Three leading voices testify on AI risk to the US Senate.
Part 1 of Evan Hubinger's 2023 lecture series on AGI safety: what the problem is, inner vs outer alignment and how to think about training safe advanced systems.
Strong entry point to a full course.

Part 3 of Hubinger's series asks how likely deceptive alignment is. He analyses whether gradient descent is more likely to find honest or deceptive models under different assumptions about inductive biases.
Rigorous argument on deceptive alignment.
Originally June 2023: Shah on DeepMind's alignment work and fairly hearing out both doomers and doubters.
Balanced take on disagreements.
A 2023 80,000 Hours episode on navigating serious philosophical confusion about the universe, decisions and moral status. Carlsmith explains why it matters for AI.
Big-picture philosophy for AI safety.

The full May 16, 2023 Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on AI oversight, with testimony from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Gary Marcus and IBM's Christina Montgomery. Altman calls for licensing of powerful models, and Marcus argues for an independent oversight agency.
The hearing where an AI CEO asked Congress to regulate his industry.

80,000 Hours (originally May 2023): Ajeya Cotra explains how standard training could accidentally teach models to deceive us. She uses her 'trillion-dollar company inherited by an eight-year-old' analogy to explain the oversight problem.
Clear explanation of deceptive alignment.

The Bankless hosts expected a crypto-style AI chat and instead got Yudkowsky's blunt case that humanity is not on track to survive superintelligence. The episode became a turning point that brought his views to a mainstream audience in early 2023.
The interview that launched the 2023 wave of public attention to AI doom.

Logan Bartlett sits down with Yudkowsky for three hours on whether humanity can survive AI. They cover his intellectual history, why he gave up hope on technical alignment in time and what might still help.
A long, personal conversation that covers his background as well as his arguments.

George Hotz and Yudkowsky hash out AI safety versus acceleration in a live debate hosted by Dwarkesh Patel. They clash over whether superintelligences would cooperate with humans and how fast AI could take off.
A lively head-to-head with a prominent accelerationist.
In a short TED talk, Yudkowsky argues that superintelligent AI could probably kill us all and that we are not ready. He explains why nobody understands what goes on inside modern AI systems.
His ten-minute summary for a general audience.

A CITRIS lecture at Berkeley in which Russell explains how not to destroy the world with AI. He argues that we should expect AI to exceed human abilities and that the standard way of building AI is unsafe.
A full lecture version of his argument after ChatGPT.
Sam Harris speaks with Russell and Gary Marcus about recent developments in AI and the long-term risks. They discuss the limits of large language models and why control matters.
Two different expert critics of current AI in one conversation.
At the Commonwealth Club, Russell looks beyond ChatGPT at the risks and rewards of AI. He explains what general-purpose AI could do for and to society and why regulation is needed.
A balanced public talk on promise and peril.

The 2023 Munk Debate on whether AI research poses an existential threat, with Bengio and Max Tegmark arguing yes against Melanie Mitchell and Yann LeCun. The two sides clash over timelines, control and current harms.
A landmark public debate between top AI scientists.
Tom Bilyeu interviews Bengio for nearly three hours on the dangers of AI and how deep learning works. Bengio explains why risks may be weirder than people think.
A long, accessible conversation for a general audience.
Bengio and Yuval Noah Harari discuss artificial intelligence, democracy and the future of civilisation. They consider how AI could affect power and public discourse.
A cross-disciplinary conversation on AI and society.
On Talk to Al Jazeera, Bengio argues that democracy is not safe in a world of powerful AI. He discusses disinformation, concentration of power and regulation.
Focuses on democratic and political risks.
In his 60 Minutes interview, Hinton warns that there is no guaranteed path to safety as AI advances. He explains why he believes AI systems understand and may soon outsmart us.
A short, high-impact introduction from the Nobel laureate.
The University of Toronto interviews Hinton shortly after he left Google about why he is worried about the future of AI. He outlines the risks he wanted to speak freely about.
His first explanations after leaving Google in 2023.
Christiane Amanpour interviews Hinton after his departure from Google about the existential threat of AI. He explains why he quit and what he fears.
A concise early interview from May 2023.
Lex Fridman interviews Tegmark about the case for halting AI development, recorded around FLI's 2023 pause letter. They cover the race dynamic, Moloch and what a pause would achieve.
His central argument from the moment of the pause letter.
DW interviews Tegmark on whether we have six months to save humanity from AI. He warns that the race is outpacing our ability to control it.
A short news interview from the pause-letter period.
At MIT Physics' 2023 event on ChatGPT, Tegmark speaks about the impact of large language models on physics research and education. He also touches on the bigger risks.
A short academic talk from MIT.
The Inside View's long interview with Krueger, then a Cambridge assistant professor. They discuss coordination, alignment research and the role of academia.
His most detailed early research interview.
Steinhardt's 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop talk on current and future challenges in aligning massive models, including emergent capabilities and deception.
A research agenda overview for alignment.
A SaTML 2023 keynote on aligning ML systems with human intent. Steinhardt covers reward hacking and oversight.
Technical keynote for ML security researchers.
A Simons Institute talk on language models as statisticians and as adapted organisms. Steinhardt discusses how to understand LLM behaviour.
Theory-flavoured view of LLMs.
A CITRIS talk on AI agents that do what we want: progress and open challenges. Dragan explains how the definition of AI's goal has changed.
Accessible overview of her alignment ideas.
The Inside View's long interview with Krakovna on AGI ruin, the sharp left turn and paradigms of AI alignment. She explains DeepMind alignment thinking.
Her most detailed interview.
Krakovna joins Cohere For AI to present paradigms of AI alignment, their components and enablers. She lays out a framework for the field.
A structured map of alignment research.
Bankless talks with Christiano, then running the Alignment Research Center, about how to prevent AI from killing us. He explains his more moderate risk estimates.
A contrast to Yudkowsky's Bankless episode.
Christiano's 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop talk lays out concrete stories of how misaligned AI systems could gradually or suddenly take control. It is short and focused on mechanisms.
A concise takeover-risk talk.
A Sydney Mathematical Research Institute talk on formalizing explanations of neural network behaviours. Christiano presents ARC's theory work.
Explains ARC's heuristic-explanations agenda.
On the FLI podcast Cotra discusses how AI could cause catastrophe. She explains her takeover scenarios.
Concise catastrophe scenarios.
At the 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop, Cotra explains why situational awareness makes measuring safety tricky. She discusses evaluation difficulties.
Key concept for AI evaluations.
Cotra talks with FLI about thinking clearly in a rapidly changing world. She shares reasoning habits for AI forecasting.
Practical epistemics for AI.
On FLI, Carlsmith discusses how we change our minds about AI risk, gut feelings versus models. He explains his updated views.
How to reason about AI risk.
A Foresight Institute session where Carlsmith discusses infinite ethics, utopia and AI. He explores implications for the far future.
Philosophical talk on long-term values.
Grace and Robin Hanson discuss AI risk on May 3, 2023, trying to find where they disagree and why. A long, careful exchange.
A model of productive disagreement.
Dwarkesh Patel interviews Karnofsky about why this could be history's most important century. They cover his Cold Takes series.
The 'Most Important Century' argument.
Dwarkesh Patel and Legg discuss why he expects AGI by 2028, superhuman alignment and new architectures.
His timelines and alignment views.
MLST interviews Shanahan on consciousness, embodiment and language models.
Deep cognitive-science discussion.
On FLI, Omohundro discusses Provably Safe Systems, the paper he co-wrote with Max Tegmark.
His main current proposal in depth.
Omohundro presents 'Provably Safe Systems: The Only Path to Controllable AGI', explaining his paper with Tegmark.
The proposal as a lecture.
CAIS seminar on discovering language model behaviours, like sycophancy and power-seeking statements, using model-written evaluations.
How to evaluate models with models.
Berkeley colloquium on RLHF progress and challenges, including hallucination and honesty.
Technical RLHF talk from its main practitioner.

Recorded weeks after the FLI pause letter, Tallinn explains on the Cognitive Revolution why he supported pausing giant AI experiments. He discusses AI risk, his investments in labs and what responsible development would require.
Tallinn's fullest explanation of the 2023 pause letter.

Dwarkesh Patel spends four hours trying to find reasons AI might not kill everyone while Yudkowsky argues back. They get into aligning LLMs, the nature of intelligence and why evolution is a warning about training.
The most rigorous stress-test of his arguments by a well-prepared interviewer.
The original 'AI Dilemma' talk by Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin, recorded March 9, 2023. They argue that the race to deploy large language models repeats social media's mistakes at far higher stakes.
The talk that brought AI risk to a mainstream audience in 2023.

Lex Fridman gives Eliezer Yudkowsky over three hours to lay out why he thinks superintelligent AI is likely to end human civilization. They cover GPT-4, why alignment is hard to get right on the first try, consciousness and advice for young people.
His most-watched long-form interview and the fullest single statement of his view.
Dwarkesh Patel asks Sutskever about timelines, alignment, leaks and life after AGI.
Concise 2023 interview with alignment content.
Olah's 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop talk on looking inside neural networks. He covers superposition and why interpretability might let us audit models for dangerous cognition.
Compact overview from the field's founder.
Opening remarks at the 2023 San Francisco Alignment Workshop on confronting the possibility of AGI.
Ilya speaking directly to alignment researchers.

Leahy discusses AI safety on the FLI podcast in early 2023, arguing that the world is fragile to large shocks and that capable AI systems could be catastrophic even without superintelligence. He also covers slowing AI down, regulation and funding models for safety research.
His 'fragile world' argument, explained step by step.
Schwartz Reisman Institute seminar version of the model-written evaluations work, with discussion of emergent risky behaviours.
Alternate, academic-audience version.
Stanford CS25 lecture on language models and human alignment: InstructGPT, why RLHF works, and the open problem of aligning systems smarter than us.
Clear classroom-level introduction from the person who led it.
A December 2022 HUJI talk on empirical challenges to theories of deep learning.
Theory of deep learning.
Hubinger lectures on risks from learned optimization at MLAB2, covering mesa-optimizers, pseudo-alignment and deceptive alignment.
Lecture version of his most-cited idea.
Richard Ngo, then at OpenAI, discusses large language models, situational awareness and striving to make the future go well.
His 80,000 Hours episode.

An early Stanford talk where Buck Shlegeris, then Redwood's CTO, introduces AI alignment and Redwood Research's approach. He explains why he works on the problem and what early empirical alignment work looked like.
See how Redwood framed its mission in its first years.

Will Jarvis talks with Buck Shlegeris, then CTO of Redwood Research, about AI safety, effective altruism and building a research organisation. A relaxed early interview that covers his path into the field.
An accessible early-career snapshot of Buck.
Jaime Sevilla talks with Jeremie Harris about projecting AI progress from compute trends, in the early days of Epoch.
Early version of Epoch's core idea.
Jaime Sevilla discusses forecasting, cultural persistence and quantum computing on Hear This Idea.
Shows his range beyond AI.
An MIT course lecture where Sarah Schwettmann, then a CSAIL postdoc, explores the meeting point of art, minds and machine learning.
Shows her neuroscience and art roots.

AXRP 13: Richard Ngo walks through his 'AGI Safety from First Principles' argument. He explains how AGI might develop goals, why those goals could be misaligned and what constraints exist on technical solutions.
Core statement of his early views.
Vanessa Kosoy discusses infra-Bayesian physicalism, a framework for agents that reason about themselves as part of the physical world.
Follow-up to the first AXRP episode.
A conversation with Vanessa Kosoy about her research on the mathematical foundations of alignment.
Informal discussion of her ideas.
Vanessa Kosoy presents and takes feedback on her alignment protocol, Precursor Detection, Classification and Assistance.
Her concrete alignment proposal.
Steve Byrnes talks with Paul Middlebrooks about brain-like AGI safety and his neuroscience-based approach.
Neuroscience-heavy discussion.

A nearly three-hour Inside View episode recorded in 2022 covering AGI meme culture, recent AI progress, timelines, 'death with dignity', EleutherAI and the founding of Conjecture. It captures Leahy's thinking just before ChatGPT.
A snapshot of Leahy's worldview from the EleutherAI era.
An Inside View interview in which Anderljung discusses regulating advanced AI, GovAI's research and how governance work can reduce catastrophic risk.
A longer early conversation on AI regulation.
A London Futurists webinar asking how we might control AI before it starts controlling us, with Dafoe among the speakers.
A wide-ranging governance discussion.
Long Inside View conversation with Rob Miles about existential risk from AI and how to explain it. Covers timelines, why alignment is hard and his path from Computerphile to his own channel.
The longest conversation with Miles about alignment.

Russell's Turing Institute lecture argues that the 'standard model' of AI (optimise a fixed objective) becomes dangerous as systems exceed human ability. He proposes human-compatible AI built around preference uncertainty.
The full argument behind his book 'Human Compatible'.
Bowman argues researchers may be under-hyping AI: underclaiming capabilities can be as harmful as overhyping when society needs to prepare.
Contrarian, well-argued take from an NLP veteran.
Nanda reads through Anthropic's 'Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits' with commentary.
Paper walkthrough for serious learners.
FLI podcast: Rohin Shah on the state of AGI safety research in 2021, from value alignment to how an AI could come to harm us and which research directions seem promising.
Field snapshot.
AXRP 16: Geoffrey Irving, who proposed AI safety via debate, discusses preparing debate for real use, including human experiments and what makes debates fair.
Deep dive on AI safety via debate.
Anna Riedl talks with Kirchner, then a Max Planck PhD researcher, about 'drug addiction' in AI, language models and scaling academia.
Early view of his ideas before OpenAI.
Brundage, then head of policy research at OpenAI, explains its policy work.
Inside OpenAI policy.
Turner presents the shard theory of human values.
Original shard theory talk.

Ethan Perez's 2022 summer-school lecture on aligning language models with human preferences. It covers why pretraining objectives don't give us what we want and how learning from human feedback helps.
Lecture-style introduction to alignment techniques.
The Inside View: Ethan Perez (Anthropic) on red-teaming language models with language models, inverse scaling (tasks where bigger models do worse) and model-written evaluations.
Good intro to his research style.
Stanford CS25 lecture treating neural network parameters as compiled programs, covering transformer circuits, induction heads and in-context learning.
Technical deep dive into transformer circuits.
Stanford seminar (May 2022) by Jacob Steinhardt (UC Berkeley): modern ML systems undergo qualitative shifts as they scale, so we must forecast and align future systems, not just today's.
A technical talk on forecasting ML progress.
Machine Learning Street Talk interviews Bengio about GFlowNets, consciousness and causality. He explains research directions toward AI that reasons more like humans.
Technical depth on his research interests before his safety pivot.
Yannic Kilcher interviews Steinhardt about 'More Is Different for AI': scaling, emergence and paperclip maximizers. Steinhardt argues future AI will be qualitatively different.
Explains his influential emergence essays.
An invited AAMAS 2022 talk on incompleteness, overoptimization and Goodhart's law. Hadfield-Menell explains why optimizing proxies fails.
The theory of why specifications break.

AXRP episode 12: Daniel Filan asks Paul Christiano why advanced AI could pose an existential risk and what safer development would look like. They go through his threat models and research agenda carefully.
Technical deep dive on AI risk.
Cotra joins FLI to discuss forecasting transformative AI with her biological anchors framework. She explains the method.
The bio-anchors report explained by its author.
A Stanford Existential Risks Initiative talk on timelines for transformative AI and language model alignment. Cotra presents her research.
Compact student-oriented talk.
A 2022 Dwarkesh Patel interview about utopia, AI and infinite ethics. Carlsmith was then at Open Philanthropy.
Philosophical depth on ethics and the future.
Carlsmith presents his report on existential risk from power-seeking AI, given in a lecture series on AI alignment. He walks through the argument's premises.
The power-seeking argument by its author.
The Inside View interviews Grace about slowing down AI and forecasting AI risk. She explains AI Impacts' research.
Her case for considering slowing AI.
A South Park Commons fireside chat on existential risk and AI apocalypse with Karnofsky. He shares his thoughts on a range of AI risk questions.
An accessible conversational intro.
A Cooperative AI Foundation seminar: AI agents may cooperate better if they don't resemble us.
Key idea in cooperative AI.
A PIBBSS talk with discussion: AI agents may cooperate better if they don't resemble us.
Extended version with discussion.
Jeffrey Ladish visits The Stoa to discuss the importance of the security mindset for personal and civilisational security.
A short early talk on his core idea.
AXRP 6: Beth Barnes explains AI safety via debate and imitative generalization, two proposals for supervising models more capable than us, including problems she found in debate experiments.
Beth's earlier scalable-oversight research, before METR.
The first AXRP episode: Adam Gleave explains adversarial policies, where RL agents learn to beat strong opponents by exploiting weird weaknesses rather than playing well.
The origin of Gleave's robustness research.
Christopher Summerfield and Sam Gershman debate how much neuroscience can contribute to AI, on Brain Inspired.
Two cognitive scientists in dialogue.
An early Towards Data Science interview with Owain Evans on predicting the future of AI and AGI.
Early Evans on forecasting.
Vanessa Kosoy explains infra-Bayesianism, her framework for decision-making when the true hypothesis is not in the agent's hypothesis class.
The standard introduction to infra-Bayesianism.

On the Towards Data Science podcast, Garfinkel discusses superhuman AI and the future of democracy and government. He explores how AI could shift power and what it could mean for political institutions.
Garfinkel on AI's long-run political effects.
A 2021 conversation between Garfinkel and political theorist Hélène Landemore, hosted with Taiwan's digital minister's office (PDIS), on AI, democracy and governance.
An unusual dialogue between AI governance and democratic theory.
A remastered introduction to AI safety from Miles's channel, explaining why powerful AI with the wrong goals could be dangerous.
The best first video for someone new to AI safety.
A long interview with Miles on AGI safety and alignment for the Machine Ethics podcast.
A thorough conversational overview.

Miles explains the 'Risks from Learned Optimization' paper: training can produce a model that is itself an optimizer with its own goal (a mesa-optimizer). That inner goal may differ from the one we trained for.
The standard explainer of inner alignment.
Towards Data Science podcast: Daniel Filan, then an AI safety PhD student at Berkeley, on peering into neural nets for safety, including his work on modularity in networks.
Daniel Filan as guest instead of host.
Rohin Shah (DeepMind) discusses threat models for misaligned AI and the main technical approaches to alignment, aimed at a technical audience new to the area.
Threat-model overview.
Dafoe and Edward Hughes present the 'Open Problems in Cooperative AI' agenda at the Alan Turing Institute, explaining why AI systems need to cooperate well with humans and each other.
Introduction to cooperative AI.
Ben Yeoh and Aschenbrenner on existential risk, economic growth and his earlier writing.
Early views on x-risk.
A September 2021 Duke Lifelong Learning session on morality in artificial intelligence.
Accessible lecture.
Jeremie Harris talks with Leike about empirical alignment research at OpenAI, recursive reward modeling and the idea of a 'minimum viable product' for alignment.
Earlier snapshot of his thinking before Superalignment.
80,000 Hours (originally Aug 2021): Chris Olah explains what is going on inside neural networks: features, circuits, and why reverse-engineering them could matter for safety.
Best long introduction to the circuits worldview.
AXRP on attainable utility preservation and his theorems on power-seeking.
Core of his technical work.
A Foresight Institute session on existential risk and existential hope, where Ord discusses both dangers and the vast potential future. It includes discussion with participants.
Balances risk with the positive vision.
Demetri Kofinas speaks with Ord on Hidden Forces about existential risks and humanity's future. They cover AI, pandemics and nuclear war.
A clear general-audience overview.
A three-hour Lex Fridman conversation on AI and physics, including Tegmark's work on using AI for science and making AI understandable. They also discuss risk and the future.
Shows his research interest in intelligible AI.
On AXRP, Daniel Filan and Hadfield-Menell discuss assistance games, the off-switch game and inverse reward design. They cover when and how AI should defer to humans.
The deepest interview on his core research.
On the Towards Data Science podcast, Jeremie Harris talks with Hadfield-Menell about humans in the loop and value alignment. They cover practical and theoretical issues.
A clear mid-level introduction.
Pieter Abbeel interviews Dragan on The Robot Brains Podcast about why Asimov's three laws need updating. They discuss human-robot interaction research.
Deep dive into her Berkeley research.

AXRP 7: Victoria Krakovna (DeepMind) on side effects: how an AI pursuing a goal can take drastic actions, and how 'impact measures' might discourage them. Connects to specification gaming and power-seeking.
The key interview on impact measures.
On AXRP, Grace discusses AI's future and impacts and why understanding them matters for preventing catastrophe.
Research-focused interview.
A Protocol Labs talk on open-source game theory at the intersection of AI and cooperation. Critch was at CHAI.
AI agents cooperating via transparency.
At the Finding the Right Abstractions Summit 2021, Critch gives 'Philosophy with a Deadline' on AI automation and human values.
Short, thoughtful talk.
Templeton World Charity Foundation conversation with ethicist Walter Sinnott-Armstrong, neuroscientist Jana Schaich Borg and Conitzer on machine morality.
Interdisciplinary team discussion.
Towards Data Science: Ethan Perez, then a PhD student who had worked at Google, Facebook and Mila, talks about making AI safe through debate and his early experiments on it.
Early view on debate.
AXRP 4: Evan Hubinger discusses 'Risks from Learned Optimization', the paper that introduced mesa-optimizers and the inner-alignment problem.
The canonical interview on mesa-optimization.
A 2021 80,000 Hours episode on worldview diversification and how big the future could be. Cotra explains Open Philanthropy's thinking.
Background on how funders reason.
Skeptics in the Pub talk: is some AI research too dangerous to publish?
Accessible publication-norms talk.
AXRP on learning human biases when inferring goals from behaviour.
Technical preference-learning episode.
2020 lecture on neural scaling laws and GPT-3.
The scaling laws lecture.
A long Palladium Magazine conversation with Tallinn on the big risks from artificial intelligence. He explains the alignment problem, coordination failures and why he prioritises existential risk.
An early, in-depth Tallinn conversation from around 2020.
A talk on the global governance of AI hosted by Altruisme Efficace France, in which Dafoe presents the challenges of governing powerful AI internationally.
Dafoe's framing of the global governance challenge.
The 2019 Montreal.AI debate between Yoshua Bengio and Gary Marcus on the future of AI, deep learning and what is missing for general intelligence.
A classic debate between two foundational figures.
TDS podcast on effective altruism, AI safety and learning human preferences from the state of the world.
His CHAI-era research.
Brundage on the societal impacts of AI and how to make them go well.
Broad societal framing.

At TEDxWarwickSalon, Jade Leung argues that governing AI is our opportunity to shape the long-term future, calling for more robust AI governance and better cooperation between governments and companies.
A short, accessible talk on why AI governance matters.
FLI conversation on inner versus outer alignment and Hubinger's survey of eleven proposals for building safe advanced AI.
Conceptual map of pre-LLM alignment proposals.
CVPR 2020 tutorial introducing circuits in convolutional neural networks: curve detectors, high-low frequency detectors and how features connect.
The original 'zoom in' circuits material, explained by its author.
A Turing Lecture at the Alan Turing Institute on 'provably beneficial AI'. Russell asks what happens if AI exceeds human decision-making and explains how assistance games keep AI deferential.
A thorough technical-but-accessible lecture on his research program.
Michael Shermer interviews Russell about his book Human Compatible and the problem of control. They discuss why the standard model of AI is flawed and how to fix it.
A relaxed book-focused conversation.
Lex Fridman interviews Bostrom on the simulation argument and superintelligence. Bostrom explains both ideas carefully and discusses how AI could change the future.
A clearer, more careful treatment of his two big ideas.
A TED conversation on the vulnerable world hypothesis: how civilisation could destroy itself and four ways we could prevent it. Bostrom explains the 'black ball' technology idea.
Introduces his vulnerable world framework.
Sam Harris speaks with Ord about preserving humanity's long-term future and the risks in The Precipice. They discuss why AI tops his list of existential risks.
The best general introduction to his existential-risk framework.
At EA Global London 2019, Ord presents The Precipice: if all goes well, human history is just beginning. He outlines the biggest existential risks.
The core ideas of The Precipice as a short talk.
Lex Fridman interviews Aaronson on computational complexity and consciousness. They discuss whether machines could be conscious.
Deep on complexity theory and mind.
Lex Fridman talks with Dragan about human-robot interaction and reward engineering. They discuss how robots should infer what people want.
Foundations of her approach to alignment.
A Robotics Today seminar, 'Optimizing Intended Reward Functions'. Dragan explains extracting the right information about human preferences.
Technical foundations of reward inference.
A Microsoft Research fireside chat between Dragan and Eric Horvitz. They discuss human-AI interaction and safe AI.
Two leading researchers in conversation.
At a Numenta research meeting, Omohundro gives a talk on GPT-3 and its implications.
Early analysis of large language models.

A recorded Q&A at Foresight Institute's 2020 AGI strategy meeting where Tallinn discusses founding CSER and FLI, his 'drill and city' model of AI development, and gaps in the AI safety ecosystem. He also explains his grantmaking process.
Tallinn explains how he thinks about funding the field.
The 2020 80,000 Hours episode released with The Precipice, covering humanity's potential futures and the risks that threaten them. Ord explains his probability estimates.
The definitive long interview on The Precipice.
An early (2019) talk by Markus Anderljung on governing transformative AI: why AI could be radically transformative and what governance research should prepare for.
An early introduction to AI governance as a field.
Ó hÉigeartaigh's talk at the 2019 Beneficial AGI conference on racing and cooperation in the development of AGI.
Why AI race narratives are dangerous.
A National University of Singapore lecture by Ó hÉigeartaigh on the future of AI and its opportunities and risks in the near and long term.
A full lecture on near- and long-term AI risk.
An early (2019) Simons Institute talk by Christiano, then at OpenAI, on aligning ML objectives with human values. It frames reward learning and oversight as the core open problems.
Historical snapshot of the agenda that became RLHF.

Stuart Russell, co-author of the standard AI textbook, introduces the alignment problem and his proposal for 'provably beneficial AI': machines that are uncertain about human preferences and learn them by watching us.
Russell's three principles in under 40 minutes.
Rohin Shah's 2019 overview of AGI safety research agendas: what different groups were working on and how the approaches fit together.
Map of the field circa 2019.
A short FLI-hosted talk in which Dafoe outlines AI strategy, policy and governance as a research field and the key problems it needs to solve.
Quick map of AI governance.
Dafoe's keynote at ESMT Berlin's Digital Society Conference 2018 on the governance of AI and its risks.
Concise governance keynote.
Olah tells Rob Wiblin how he reached top AI labs without an undergraduate degree, plus his views on research taste, Distill and interpretability.
Inspiring, unconventional career story.

Lex Fridman talks with Russell about the long-term future of AI, the control problem and his idea of AI that is uncertain about human objectives. They also discuss AlphaGo, autonomous weapons and the history of the field.
An early, wide-ranging introduction to his human-compatible approach.
Joe Rogan talks with Bostrom for two and a half hours, mostly about the simulation argument plus AI and existential risk. Rogan's struggle to grasp the simulation argument became famous.
His most-watched long conversation.
A short talk on moral artificial intelligence for the McGowan Fund.
Intro to moral AI.
Originally from March 2019: OpenAI's Jack Clark, Amanda Askell and Miles Brundage on whether policy can keep up with AI, including GPT-2's staged release.
Historic OpenAI policy team conversation.
Garfinkel's EA Global London 2018 talk 'How sure are we about this AI stuff?', making the case for measured scepticism about prioritising AI risk. It prompted wide debate in the AI safety community.
The talk that sparked a major debate on AI risk arguments.
Miles explains the orthogonality thesis: intelligence and goals are independent, so a very smart AI can have any goal.
A foundational idea in AI risk, clearly explained.
A long interview with Ó hÉigeartaigh on whether AI is a problem or a promise.
A balanced, accessible overview.
Bowman's 2018 IPAM talk on natural language semantics in learned representations, from his pre-safety NLP research.
Context on his NLP background.
Brundage and Tim Hwang on AI policy and public perception at Y Combinator.
Early policy discussion.

80,000 Hours conversation (originally released Oct 2018) on solving alignment and handing the future to AI. Christiano explains iterated amplification and why getting help from AI on hard questions is the core problem.
Classic explanation of his early agenda.
Dafoe's 2018 80,000 Hours episode on defusing political and economic risks from existing AI, including inequality, surveillance and great-power competition.
Early AI governance agenda.
An early Lex Fridman episode with Bengio on deep learning, its history and its limits. It predates his safety focus but shows how he thinks about intelligence.
Background on the science that made modern AI possible.
The very first Lex Fridman podcast episode, with Tegmark discussing his book Life 3.0 and the future of AI. They cover consciousness, AGI and beneficial AI.
A historic conversation on Life 3.0.
Tegmark's 2018 TED talk on how to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI. He outlines a hopeful future that requires wisdom and safety work.
An early optimistic framing of AI safety.
At Talks at Google, Tegmark presents Life 3.0: Being Human in the Age of AI. He discusses what kind of future we should aim for.
The book talk for Life 3.0.
A 2018 80,000 Hours episode on forecasting future technology and how much to trust expert predictions. Grace discusses the earlier AI survey.
Classic episode on expert forecasts.
A 2018 80,000 Hours episode on times philanthropy transformed the world and Open Philanthropy's plans. Karnofsky explains the reasoning behind funding AI safety.
Background on why AI safety got funded.
80,000 Hours episode on how to become an AI alignment researcher, with Leike (then at DeepMind) on skills, PhDs and the state of the field in 2018.
Career advice from a field founder.
Rob Miles explains on Computerphile why adding an off switch to a general AI is not simple. An agent with almost any goal has reasons to stop you pressing it, or to make you press it.
A classic explainer of the off-switch problem.
A 2017 NYU debate between Yann LeCun and Marcus on whether AI needs more innate machinery.
The famous LeCun–Marcus debate.
A CSER Cambridge talk by Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh on taking the long run seriously in AI, introducing long-term risks from advanced AI.
An early talk from CSER's founding director.
At GoCAS in Gothenburg in September 2017, Grace presents empirical evidence on the future of AI. An early research talk.
Early empirical forecasting work.
The very first 80,000 Hours podcast (2017): Miles Brundage, then at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute, on the world's need for AI strategists and policy experts.
Classic AI policy career episode.

In the follow-up, Miles looks at a promising answer to the stop-button problem: an AI that is uncertain about human preferences and so lets humans correct it (Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning). He also covers its limits.
Shows how researchers actually try to solve corrigibility.
Omohundro's machine learning keynote at TiEcon 2017.
Industry keynote.

At Talks at Google in 2017, Soares, then MIRI's executive director, explains MIRI's work on ensuring smarter-than-human AI has positive outcomes. He outlines the technical problems MIRI thought needed solving.
A window into MIRI's research agenda before the LLM era.

In his TED talk Russell offers three principles for building safer AI: the machine's only goal is human preferences, it is uncertain what they are, and it learns them from our behaviour. He uses the off-switch problem to show why this matters.
The shortest clear statement of his core idea.
Y Combinator interviews Shanahan, scientific adviser on Ex Machina, about AI and the film.
Fun intro via Ex Machina.
At the 2016 Cambridge Conference on Catastrophic Risk, Krakovna gives a talk on AI safety's past, present and future. She surveys the field's growth.
A historical snapshot of early AI safety.
Leike presents his PhD-era work on general reinforcement learning (AIXI-style agents) at MIRI's 2016 Colloquium Series on Robust and Beneficial AI.
For theory fans: where his alignment interest began.

A 2016 Stanford distinguished-speaker talk in which Yudkowsky explains why aligning a powerful AI is technically hard and where research should start. He walks through utility functions, the shutdown problem and why a smarter agent's moves are hard to predict.
The classic technical introduction to the alignment problem, years before ChatGPT.
At MIRI's 2016 colloquium series, Hadfield-Menell presents the off-switch game. He shows why uncertainty about objectives makes AI accept being switched off.
The original off-switch result explained by its author.
At MIRI's 2016 colloquium series, Christiano presents on training an aligned RL agent. An early look at his alignment proposals.
Historical early alignment work.
At EAG 2016, Critch, then at MIRI, describes logical induction, a new model of deductively limited reasoning.
The logical induction result explained.
A Future of Humanity Institute talk on superintelligence: could we create smarter beings and what would it mean? An early Critch talk.
Early introduction to the topic.
A TEDx talk on what's happening with AI and robotics as big tech invests billions.
Short 2016 overview.

A 2015 MIT Center for Brains, Minds and Machines lecture in which Tallinn presents the problem of global coordination around powerful technology. It shows his early thinking on AI risk and cooperation.
An early, foundational talk from 2015.

Hosted by Cambridge's Centre for the Study of Existential Risk in 2015, Russell lectures on the long-term future of artificial intelligence. It is one of his earliest public explanations of why success in AI could be a problem.
A historic talk from when few academics took AI risk seriously.
Bostrom's 2015 TED talk asks what happens when computers get smarter than we are. He argues we need to solve the control problem before we create superintelligence.
The classic short introduction to superintelligence risk.
A 2015 CSER seminar where Ord compares natural and human-caused extinction risks. He argues anthropogenic risks dominate.
The early reasoning behind his risk rankings.
A February 2015 CSER seminar, 'Minds Like Ours: An Approach to AI Risk', by Shanahan.
An early academic take on AI risk.
An Oxford Martin School talk by Muehlhauser on containing the intelligence explosion and the role of transparency.
A rare lecture from MIRI's early leadership.
At Talks at Google in 2014, Bostrom presents Superintelligence: what happens when machines surpass humans in general intelligence. He explains paths to superintelligence and the control problem.
The original book talk that shaped the field.
Singularity Weblog interviews Omohundro on envisioning who we are and where we want to go with AI.
Classic interview on AI drives.
A 2013 interview with Muehlhauser, then at MIRI, on AI and the intelligence explosion.
An early look at MIRI's arguments.
Muehlhauser, then at the Singularity Institute, speaks on superhuman artificial intelligence.
A short early talk on superhuman AI.
A 2013 interview in which Shulman discusses whether untrustworthy human brain emulations could be used to build trustworthy AI.
An early, unusual Shulman interview.
At the 2010 Singularity Summit, Legg presents his work on measuring machine intelligence.
Early formal thinking on AGI.
